clue.text: American base abroad getting single-cell specimens from US

indicators.note: something abroad has wandered away from its home spot, so the word base is scattered into a new order

parts.note: AM is the standard abbreviation for American
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A US military base overseas is the source of some laboratory samples of single-celled life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From US' tells the solver to use the American spelling, without the O of the British amoebas.
explanation.definitionFit: Amebas are single-celled organisms; the plural fits 'specimens', and the spelling is the American one.

clue.text: Expression of contempt about flipping sea captain

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the combined letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a scornful exclamation
A is a dictionary abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Someone snorts in disgust at a sea captain who has lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads like a mild curse aimed at the captain, but it turns BAH plus A upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahab is the obsessed whaling captain of Melville's novel Moby-Dick, so a famous fictional sea captain.

clue.text: Makes less of computer records out of line

parts.note: a minicomputer, a mid-sized machine

indicators.note: out of here means without, so the named letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: files are kept records
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Computer records that are out of order get played down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of line' reads as misbehaving, but splits into a deletion signal and the letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To minify is to belittle or lessen, so minifies means makes less of something.

clue.text: Gypsy inside waits for boring types

indicators.note: inside says the first word sits within the word that follows it

parts.note: bides means waits or stays
a Rom is a Romany man

explanation.surface: A traveller hangs around waiting for some dull people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests drilling, but here means tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a tiresome, commonplace person or remark, from the sedative drug; so bromides are bores.

clue.text: Very large retiring relative touching bottom of mattress springs!

indicators.note: the relative retires, withdrawing from the word for very large

parts.note: spanking, as in 'a spanking great house', means very large
kin are relatives

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its last letter is S

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a big family member landing on the bed and setting its springs bouncing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' takes KIN out of SPANKING to leave SPANG, and 'bottom of' mattress adds S. Spang is a Scots verb meaning leap, so the definition is a verb, not the bed springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Spang is a Scots and dialect word meaning to leap or bound, so spangs means leaps.

clue.text: Cheers for model

parts.note: pro means in favour of
to sit is to pose as a model

explanation.surface: A toast raised to a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin drinking toast, the equivalent of the English cheers.

clue.text: Many years following pub darts

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the years go second, behind the pub

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
eons are vast stretches of time

explanation.surface: Darts have been played in the pub for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darts' is not the pub game, which the surface paints, but a plural noun meaning arrowheads.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheon is the barbed head of a dart or arrow in heraldry, so pheons are darts.

clue.text: Artist's agent is rough

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword artist
a secret agent

explanation.surface: A painter's agent turns out to be a tough customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Raspy describes a harsh, grating texture or voice, which is a rough one.

clue.text: Rock group's work not moving at all

parts.note: the Rolling Stones, the rock band
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A famous rock band's latest output has ground to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as belonging, with STONES followed directly by TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-still is an idiom for completely motionless, as still as a stone.

clue.text: Noisette moved from grass

indicators.note: letters that have been moved are shifted out of place, so they appear in a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, a hazelnut-flavoured chocolate or a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A nut chocolate shifted off the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Teosinte is a tall Central American grass, the wild ancestor of maize.

clue.text: Ministers urge river work on English county

parts.note: hie is an old verb for urge on or hasten
R is the abbreviation for river
OP is short for opus, a work
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, a county on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Clergy are pressing for river works in a county of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierophant was a priest who interpreted sacred mysteries, so a religious minister.

clue.text: Monastery officer in rare upset about business

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the word for business
the letters of 'in rare' are upset, knocked into a new order

parts.note: a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Something unusual has gone wrong with a company's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the material that is 'upset', and 'about' wraps that around the business word.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirmarer is the monk in charge of a monastery's infirmary, its sick ward.

clue.text: Love Tessa playing in second movement

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the word for second

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a second

indicators.note: the letters are playing, moving about into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic message to Tessa, who is performing in the second movement of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' gives O, and 'playing' rearranges O plus TESSA to AESTOS, which goes 'in' MO. The music in the surface hides that 'movement' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso, meaning majestic, is a tempo marking that also names a stately passage of music.

clue.text: Worker behind heap of waste with no end of pong?

definitions.text: Worker behind heap of waste with no end of pong?

indicators.note: behind puts the worker after the heap in the answer
with no means lacking, so the named letter is dropped from the heap
end of points to the last letter of the smell word as the one to drop

parts.note: bing is a Scots word for a heap, especially of mining waste
the final letter of pong, the one to remove
a man is a workman or employee

explanation.surface: A refuse collector stands behind a rubbish heap that has stopped smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: someone who works behind a waste heap, which with the G gone is literally a bin. A pong is a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A binman is a British refuse collector, whose job is clearing heaps of waste.

clue.text: Gives a view over trees

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
pines are trees

explanation.surface: Something offers a vista across woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives a view' suggests scenery, but it means states an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, so opines means expresses one's view.

clue.text: Addition exercise starts with four and five — nine!

indicators.note: to exercise is to put through movements, so the opening letters are moved around
starts are the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the opening letters of four, and, five
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sum set as homework: four and five makes nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Addition exercise' reads as one phrase, a sum; the arithmetic 4 + 5 = 9 is correct but irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: An affix is something attached to a word or object, so an addition.

clue.text: Silver notches left out in clasps

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: out means removed, so the named letter is taken from the notches

parts.note: raffle is a dictionary verb meaning to notch or serrate, used here as a noun plural
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Silver fastenings have had their notches missed out.
explanation.definitionFit: An agraffe is a hooked clasp or fastening, so agraffes are clasps.

clue.text: Hymn fades with one listener looking skywards

parts.note: dies away means fades
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: looking skywards faces up, so in this down entry the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the ear is what listens

explanation.surface: A hymn trails away as a lone member of the audience gazes upward.
explanation.walkthrough: EAR turned upward becomes RAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dies Irae, Latin for day of wrath, is the medieval hymn sung in the Requiem Mass.

clue.text: German behind football club not a City type

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the German goes second, following the club

parts.note: Aston Villa, the Birmingham football club
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German supports a football team, not one of the City sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like a rival team, such as Manchester City, but means a town as opposed to a village.
explanation.definitionFit: A villager lives in a village, a rural settlement, so is not a city dweller.

clue.text: Terror group around London area in racket, taking land illegally

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the group's letters wrap the London area

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: in places that combination inside the racket

parts.note: the jihadist group
SE is the postcode for south-east London

explanation.surface: A terrorist outfit on a London patch runs a criminal racket and seizes property.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: the London area goes inside the terror group, and that inside the racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Disseisin is the legal term for wrongful dispossession of someone's freehold land.

clue.text: Early bumper passes over retreating club bat

indicators.note: passes over means spans across, so the bumper's letters stretch round the club

parts.note: rouse is an old word for a bumper, a full glass drunk as a toast

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the club's letters run backwards

parts.note: a mere is a Maori war club

explanation.surface: An old car fender skims over a golf club in reverse and hits a bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' flags that bumper is used in an archaic sense, a brimming glass drunk as a toast, not a car part.
explanation.definitionFit: Reremouse is an archaic word for a bat, the flying mammal.

clue.text: Type of shellfish from European country mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so the country is taken by its sound

parts.note: the country, said out loud

explanation.surface: A kind of shellfish imported from a country in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostrea is the genus of true oysters, so a type of shellfish.

clue.text: African party in resort as before showing interest in literature

indicators.note: in places the party letters inside the word for resort

parts.note: to resort to something is to use it
the African National Congress

explanation.surface: A South African political party holds a conference at a seaside resort, as it did previously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' warns that the meaning is an old one; usance in the sense of interest on money is found in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Usance once meant interest charged on a loan, a sense found in older literature such as The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Huge old man first up

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: Mr is the title for a man
number one is first

explanation.surface: A massive veteran is the first to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: MR ONE runs upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Enorm is an obsolete form of enormous, so an old word meaning huge.

clue.text: Recalled Beethoven dedicatee's acidy stuff

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Für Elise is Beethoven's famous piano piece dedicated to Elise

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a woman Beethoven wrote music for, and her sour concoction.
explanation.definitionFit: Esile is a Spenserian word for vinegar, which is acidic.

clue.text: Gossip after Liechtenstein show off

indicators.note: after puts the gossip second, behind the country's code

parts.note: FL is Liechtenstein's international vehicle registration code
an aunt is stock for a chattering busybody

explanation.surface: Someone flaunts it after hearing the gossip from Liechtenstein.
explanation.walkthrough: Gossip is usually a person here, not talk: the chattering aunt is a crossword stock figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to display ostentatiously, which is to show off.

clue.text: Gala is organised by some of Daphne's family

indicators.note: organised means arranged anew, so the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A party is being thrown by Daphne's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Daphne is not a woman but a shrub genus, in the same plant family as the eaglewood trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Agila is eaglewood, a tree in the Thymelaeaceae, the plant family that also includes Daphne.

clue.text: Australian detectives turned up in Queensland plant

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for Australian
DIs are detective inspectors

explanation.definitionFit: Sida is a genus of mallow plants, one being Queensland hemp, a weed of that Australian state.

clue.text: Refrained from supporting Asian island endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means with no end, so the island loses its final letter

parts.note: for means in support of
the large island of south-east Asia

explanation.definitionFit: Forborne is the past participle of forbear, meaning to hold back or abstain.

clue.text: Old-fashioned stuffing recipe not normally written down

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are stuffing, filling, the word for old-fashioned

parts.note: something old-fashioned is dated

indicators.note: the letters of recipe are set out not in their normal order

explanation.definitionFit: In accounting, an asset written down has had its book value reduced, which is what depreciated means.

clue.text: Spirit in station swelling

clue.text: Cut back around elevated red room with seats

around means the reversed word surrounds the rearranged colour

parts.note: to axe is to cut

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone trims back a raised red room full of chairs.
